subject: Stable streaming cutover itinerary & checklist
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@avahealth.com>, sre@avahealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stable streaming cutover itinerary & checklist

Hi Sara / Ava SRE team —

Thanks again for partnering with us on the streaming + function-calling launch. Attached is a concise implementation checklist and the proposed JSON schema for structured outputs (streaming-json-schema-v2.json). Key asks from our side before we cut traffic to the streaming endpoint: 

- Confirm network egress allowlist (we've attached network_allowlist.txt with Redwood IP ranges).
- Confirm token scope and rotation cadence for the service account.
- Provide a 2-hour maintenance window for the canary cutover (we propose Friday 2028-08-04 02:00–04:00 UTC).
- Share the final SRE contact for on-call during cutover.

Proposed plan in brief:
1) Dry run of streaming connection and schema validation (non-prod) — Tue 2028-08-01
2) Canary cutover (1% -> 10% traffic, automated rollback) — Fri 2028-08-04 window above
3) Full cut to stable routing after 24h of metrics green — Sat 2028-08-05

I've pulled in Monica (CS lead) for the mutual action plan and Ben / Jonas for technical runbook details. Please let us know availability for a 30-min kickoff tomorrow.

Attachments: implementation_checklist.xlsx, streaming-json-schema-v2.json, network_allowlist.txt

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@avahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: sre@avahealth.com, tom.ellis@avahealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stable streaming cutover itinerary & checklist

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear plan and checklist. High level: we can support the 02:00–04:00 UTC window on 2028-08-04. A few notes from our side before the dry run: 

- I'll have our SRE (Tom Ellis) confirm the allowlist and share any internal firewall ticket numbers.
- For token rotation, we need guidance for scoped keys for streaming vs control-plane calls; can Ben outline minimal scopes?
- We prefer a canary ramp of 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% (shorter steps) rather than 1% -> 10%. Is that compatible with automatic batching behavior?

I'm available for the 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Director of Product, Ava Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@avahealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 13:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stable streaming cutover itinerary & checklist — technical notes

Sara — quick answers inline: 

- Token scopes: create two API tokens (or service account credentials) 
  * streaming: scope "stream.write" + "stream.read" (restricted to the streaming route)
  * management: scope "models.read" + "routes.admin"
  We'll send a short token-scope.txt template you can use.

- Canary ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% is fine. The runtime's adaptive batching will try to preserve latency SLOs during the ramp; we'll pin a per-route batch ceiling to prevent latency spikes.

- Network allowlist: confirm the attached network_allowlist.txt includes the CIDR ranges you need; if your firewall cannot accept host-level entries, we can provide region-based ranges.

Technical runbook highlights (attached):
- Pre-cut validations: schema validator run against 1000 historical messages, KV prefix cache primed with sample traffic.
- Canary metrics: 95th/99th latency, error rate, token cost delta, structured output validation pass rate.
- Automatic fallback: if error rate > 1% or 99th latency increases by > 200ms for 10m, rollback to previous routing.

Attachments referenced: network_allowlist.txt, token-scope.txt, implementation_checklist.xlsx

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stable streaming cutover itinerary & checklist — canary config

Ben / team —

Couple of implementation notes from infra: 

> On Tue, Jul 25, 2028 at 1:09 PM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Canary metrics: 95th/99th latency, error rate, token cost delta, structured output validation pass rate.

We'll add a lightweight tracing hook to tag canary requests (x-rdw-canary: true) so we can slice metrics in the console. For this customer I recommend the following canary config: 
- Step 1: 0.5% (30m)
- Step 2: 5% (60m)
- Step 3: 20% (2h)

We should also pre-warm the KV cache by replaying ~10k sample requests (non-prod). I'll coordinate with Tom (Ava SRE) on sample payloads.

I'll draft the rollout playbook and upload to the Drive link you have.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
